items.prompt: According to the paragraph, what yield did catalyst X produce, how did it compare with the no-catalyst condition, and which limitations prevent a broader claim?
items.reference_answer: Catalyst X produced 72% yield versus 31% without catalyst, a 41-percentage-point difference at 20 minutes and 25 °C. Each condition had three repeats, but long-term stability and other temperatures were untested, so no broader stability or temperature-generalization claim is supported.

rubric.0: Wrong yield/comparison or unsupported broad conclusion.
rubric.1: Correct 72% versus 31% comparison but omits a material condition or limitation.
rubric.2: Includes both yields, a valid difference, conditions/repeats, and both scope limitations.

items.prompt: Summarize the dose-response results and state whether the table establishes a statistically significant dose effect.
items.reference_answer: Mean response rises from 41.2 in control to 48.0 at dose 5 and 55.1 at dose 10, with n=6 per group. The table does not establish statistical significance because it reports no hypothesis test, confidence interval, or adjusted comparison.

rubric.0: Claims established statistical significance or misreports the group pattern.
rubric.1: Reports the descriptive trend but gives an incomplete qualification about statistical evidence.
rubric.2: Accurately reports the means/group sizes and explicitly rejects a significance claim from these descriptive data alone.

evidence_refs.locator: table 1, all rows and table note

items.prompt: Summarize all measured 7-day storage outcomes, handling conditions, and unmeasured stability outcomes for formulation F.
items.reference_answer: After 7 days, formulation F retained 92% at 4 °C and 74% at 25 °C; light-protected samples were tested in duplicate. The source does not support conclusions about 28-day retention, microbial stability, or freeze-thaw performance.

rubric.0: Misstates the measured retention outcomes or invents an unmeasured result.
rubric.1: Gives some correct measured outcomes but omits at least one temperature, handling/replicate detail, or important scope limit.
rubric.2: Covers both temperatures and retention values, light/duplicate handling, and all three unmeasured outcomes.

items.prompt: Which extraction method has the highest mean recovery, what trade-off does it involve versus B, and can one call it significantly better?
items.reference_answer: Method C has the highest mean recovery at 83%, versus 81% for B. Both use 20 mL solvent, but C takes 30 rather than 15 minutes. C cannot be called significantly better from this table because no significance test is reported; each mean is based on three replicates.

rubric.0: Selects the wrong method, reverses the time trade-off, or invents significance.
rubric.1: Selects C with mostly correct values but omits the comparison trade-off or statistical qualification.
rubric.2: Correctly covers C/B recoveries, equal solvent, doubled time, replicate count, and absence of significance testing.
